I have been farming these 9.5 mu in Quzhou for thirty years, and I know every corner of my land. With seven people in the house and some of the younger ones working off-farm, I cannot afford to waste labor or time. The wheat-maize double crop is the only system that makes sense here—it is what this soil and climate were made for, and it puts food on the table and cash in hand.

For wheat, I will plant an improved variety in early October. I trust the improved seeds because they are reliable against the diseases we see here and give me steady yields. I will rotary till the field before sowing to get a good seedbed, put down about 14 kg of nitrogen per mu split between base and jointing/topdressing, and irrigate three times: once before winter to help the crop establish, once at jointing in spring, and once during grain filling. I will spray herbicide and do one or two fungicide/insecticide passes as needed.

For maize, the window after wheat harvest in early June is tight. To save time and keep moisture in the ground, I will use no-tillage seeding directly into the wheat stubble. I will plant a hybrid maize—nothing else makes sense anymore because the hybrids outyield the old types by too much to ignore. I will apply similar fertilizer rates as wheat, irrigate twice at the critical stages (jointing and tasseling/silking), and spray for weeds and corn borers. I keep my nitrogen around 14 kg per mu for each crop; I have learned that more than that often just lodges the wheat or wastes money, and less hurts the yield.
